rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **If tan θ > 1** (θ > 45°): this bisector is the **obtuse** angle bisector  ·  **Worked check:** slope of Bisector 1 (6x + 6y − 1 = 0) is m_b = −6/6 = −1; with the original line's slope m₁ = −1/2: tan θ = |(−1/2 − (−1))/(1 + (−1/2)(−1))| = |(1/2)/(3/2)| = 1/3

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: As a cross-check, find the angle θ between one of the original lines and one candidate bisector using: tan θ = |(m₁ − m_b)/(1 + m₁·m_b)|, where m₁ is the original line's slope and m_b is the bisector's slope  ·  **If tan θ < 1** (θ < 45°): since θ is half the angle between the two original lines, the total angle is less than 90°, so this bisector is the **acute** angle bisector

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Since tan θ = 1/3 < 1, this confirms 6x + 6y − 1 = 0 is definitively the **acute angle bisector** — matching the a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ method
